note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Latvia: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: A Latvian resident pays personal income tax of 25.5% on annual income up to the social-insurance cap (€105,300) and 33% above, plus 3% on total income over €200,000, after a fixed non-taxable minimum of €550 a month in 2026 (€6,600 a year), rising to €570 a month from 2027; there is no municipal income tax.
figures.applies: Settled 2026-11-01 from the amending law in Latvijas Vēstnesis: transitional provision 197 sets €550 a month for 2026 (PwC agrees); article 12(1) sets €570, which applies from 2027 (the figure Deloitte gave for 2026). The 105,300 cap is the maximum contribution base of the social insurance law, read from PwC.

sources.said: 1) 25,5 procenti — gada ienākuma daļai, kas nepārsniedz likumā "Par valsts sociālo apdrošināšanu" noteikto obligāto iemaksu objekta maksimālo apmēru; 2) 33 procenti — gada ienākuma daļai, kas pārsniedz
Nodokļa papildu likme, kas jāmaksā rezumējošā kārtībā no kopējā šā panta otrajā daļā noteiktā taksācijas gada ienākumu pārsnieguma virs 200 000 euro , ir trīs procenti.
Mēneša neapliekamais minimums ir 570 euro mēnesī.
Piemērojot šā likuma 12. panta pirmo daļu, mēneša neapliekamais minimums: 1) 2025. gadā ir 510 euro mēnesī; 2) 2026. gadā ir 550 euro mēnesī.
A rate of 25.5% applies to income up to EUR 105,300. Any income over EUR 105,300 attracts a rate of 33%.
An additional 3% PIT rate applies to the portion of an individual's total annual income that exceeds EUR 200,000.
There are no local taxes on income, such as municipal taxes.
The employer is required to apply a fixed personal allowance (FPA) of EUR 550 ( EUR 6,600 per year) , regardless of individual's income level.

figures.finding: An employee pays 10.5% and the employer 23.59% in national social insurance contributions on income up to €105,300 a year; a self-employed person pays 31.07%, and may pay 10% on income below the minimum; above the cap a solidarity tax at the same rates applies (effective 25%).
figures.applies: 2026. A payer of royalties to a resident individual also pays 10% NSIC.

sources.said: Employer 23.59 Employee 10.50
Income on which NSIC is calculated is capped at EUR 105,300.
Self-employed 31.07
In addition, 10% NSIC is payable by a payer of royalty to Latvian-resident individuals (living in Latvia).
However, the effective ST rate is 25%.

figures.finding: The employer withholds 25.5% from monthly pay up to €8,775 (one twelfth of €105,300); a payer of royalties to an individual not registered as self-employed withholds 25% of the gross.
figures.applies: 2026; royalty regime extended to the end of 2027.

sources.said: The employer applies a 25.5% PIT on monthly gross income of up to EUR 8,775.
Latvian employers are required to withhold income tax on employment income paid to employees and remit the tax to the tax authorities.

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed on Latvian-source income; royalties paid to a non-resident individual bear 25.5% withholding unless a treaty reduces it.
figures.applies: No artistes' rule was found; employment income is taxed through the employer as for residents.

sources.said: Non-residents are liable to income tax on their Latvian-source income.
Royalties paid to nonresident individuals are subject to a 25.5% withholding tax, unless the rate is reduced under an applicable tax treaty.

figures.finding: Royalties paid to an individual not registered as self-employed are taxed by 25% withholding on the gross with no notional expense deduction (regime extended to the end of 2027), and the payer adds 10% NSIC.

sources.said: For the individuals who are not registered as self-employed persons and payment is treated as royalties, the payer of royalties must apply 25% tax on the gross royalties via withholding, without applying a notional expense rate.

figures.finding: VAT is 21%; a person whose taxable supplies exceed €50,000 in a calendar year must register.

sources.said: The standard VAT rate on supplies of goods and services is 21%.
Persons whose taxable supplies (excluding imports) exceed EUR 50,000 in a calendar year must register for VAT purposes.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; the return is filed 1 March to 1 June of the next year (1 April to 1 July above €105,300), with tax due by 23 June (23 July).

sources.said: Income tax returns should be filed individually on a calendar-year basis between 1 March and 1 June in the year following the year of assessment.
Additional tax not exceeding EUR 640 is payable by 23 June or 23 July, depending on the annual tax return filing deadline.
